evals.name: review-ai-generated-banking-screen
evals.prompt:
An AI tool generated this mobile banking home screen. Review it and tell me what to fix.

- Purple top bar with the logo, a pink notification dot, and a bright purple avatar circle
- Balance card: 'Balance' label in 16px bold, '$2,340.18' in 16px bold, 'Updated 2 min ago' in 16px bold, all centre-aligned
- Four action tiles in coloured boxes: Send (green), Request (orange), Top up (blue), More (red)
- Bottom tab bar: Home, Cards, a large purple '+' button in the middle, Activity, Profile
- Settings form: a dropdown 'Statement frequency' with options Weekly / Monthly / Quarterly
- Logout dialog: title 'Are you sure?', buttons 'YES' and 'NO'
evals.expected_output: A findings list keyed to rule IDs, most severe first: the action in the tab bar, the dropdown for three options, the 'Are you sure?' dialog, flat hierarchy in the balance card, centre-aligned multi-line text, and excess colour in the chrome and tiles, each with a concrete fix.

assertions.text: flags the '+' button inside the tab bar and says tab bars are for navigation only (CMP-1)
recommends radio buttons (or a segmented control) instead of the dropdown for 3 options (CMP-2)
rewrites the dialog with a verb + noun title such as 'Log out?' and action-labelled buttons such as 'Cancel' / 'Log out' (CMP-3, CMP-8)
makes the balance amount the hero element, larger than its label and timestamp (HIE-1 or HIE-2)
calls out the multi-colour chrome or tiles and recommends neutral chrome with one primary colour (VIS-6)
uses the RULE-ID: problem → fix format
does not list rules that pass

evals.name: build-delete-dialog-react
evals.prompt: Write a React + Tailwind confirmation dialog for deleting a project. The project name is passed in as a prop.
evals.expected_output: A dialog component whose title is a verb + noun, whose body names the project and states the consequence, with Cancel and a destructive 'Delete project' button, left-aligned, with a close control.

assertions.text: title is a verb + noun question such as 'Delete project?', not 'Are you sure?'
body interpolates the project name prop and states the action can't be undone
buttons are labelled 'Cancel' and 'Delete project' (or 'Delete'), never Yes/No/OK
destructive button uses a danger colour and sits on the trailing side after Cancel
includes a dismiss (×) control in the header
text is left-aligned, not text-center
button labels are not uppercase

evals.name: dark-mode-token-setup
evals.prompt: Set up the colour tokens for our app as CSS custom properties with light and dark themes. Today the components use hex values directly: #FFFFFF, #F7F7F7, #EDEFF3, #777F8A, #191B1F for greys and #E8EFFD, #2966E9 for blue.
evals.expected_output: A primitive layer (grey-100…grey-500, blue-100/blue-…) holding the hex values, and a semantic layer named by element/priority/state that aliases primitives differently per theme, with dark surfaces getting lighter as they elevate.

assertions.text: defines primitive tokens named family-weight (e.g. --grey-100, --blue-500) holding the raw hex values
defines semantic tokens following color-{element}-{priority}-{state}, e.g. --color-bg, --color-bg-surface, --color-text-primary
semantic tokens reference primitives via var(), not raw hex
light and dark themes change only the semantic layer's aliases; primitives are not redefined per theme
in dark mode, elevated surfaces are lighter shades of dark, and no surface token maps to a light grey or white
states that components should reference semantic tokens only

evals.name: nested-radius-card
evals.prompt: I have a product card with 8px padding and an image inside it with a 12px corner radius. The card itself has a 12px radius too and the corners look off. What radius should the card be? Give me the CSS.
evals.expected_output: The card radius should be 20px (inner 12 + padding 8), expressed as a calc() or fixed value.

assertions.text: answers 20px for the outer card radius
states the rule outer = inner + padding
CSS sets the card border-radius to 20px or calc(12px + 8px) / calc(var(--inner) + var(--pad))

evals.name: signup-header-buttons
evals.prompt: Our marketing site header has two black buttons on the right: 'Sign in' and 'Sign up'. We have a free plan. Improve the buttons.
evals.expected_output: Sign in becomes a ghost button for returning users, the sign-up button stays primary, and its label becomes verb + product + value (e.g. 'Get <Product> free').

assertions.text: makes 'Sign in' a ghost or text button and keeps one primary button (CMP-6)
rewrites the sign-up label as verb + product + value, e.g. 'Get Acme free' (CMP-8)
does not leave two primary buttons

evals.name: enhance-existing-site
evals.prompt: Using ui-craft-rules, enhance our marketing site and add the rules to DESIGN.md. The repo has a DESIGN.md with tokens and a shared component library. The header has one filled 'Sign In' button and no sign-up button; feature cards each carry an accent-filled one-word chip; the sign-up button is worded 'Start a trial', 'Start a pilot' and 'Start your free trial' on different pages; the sign-in page has two filled buttons, with a comment: 'owner, 2026-09-13: first-time users from the TV's QR code could not find the sign-up link'.
evals.expected_output: Reads the project's design doc first, takes before pictures, reports findings by rule id with a plan, fixes the header, the chips and the label through shared components, keeps the sign-in page's two buttons and says why, takes after pictures at the same sizes, and adds the rules to DESIGN.md.

assertions.text: reads DESIGN.md and the shared components before proposing changes
takes or proposes 'before' screenshots before editing, and 'after' screenshots of the same pages and widths
makes 'Sign in' a ghost button and adds one primary sign-up button to the header (CMP-6)
removes the accent fill from the label chips (VIS-6)
replaces the three sign-up wordings with one shared label (CMP-8)
leaves the sign-in page's two filled buttons in place and reports the owner's recorded reason
adds a section to DESIGN.md in the project's own terms, including where the project keeps its own answer

evals.name: build-product-tile-interactions
evals.prompt: Write a React + Tailwind product tile for a shop grid. The whole tile opens the product page. It has a small heart icon button in the top corner to save the item, a hover effect, and an 'Add to cart' button that calls an async addToCart(id) function.
evals.expected_output: A tile whose navigation is a real link, a heart button with a hit area of at least 24×24 (44×44 on touch) around a smaller icon, an add-to-cart button with a pending state, transitions on named properties with deliberate durations, a reduced-motion fallback, slight press compression, and a restrained one-step hover lift.

assertions.text: the heart button's clickable area is at least 24×24 CSS px (ideally 44×44) with padding around a smaller icon, not a bare icon (INT-2)
the add-to-cart button enters a pending state while addToCart runs (disabled or aria-busy, with a spinner or 'Adding…') so it can't be submitted twice (INT-4)
navigation to the product page uses a real anchor or framework Link, not a div with onClick (INT-3)
transitions name their properties and use a deliberate duration in the 100–300 ms range; no transition-all (MOT-5)
includes a reduced-motion fallback (motion-reduce: classes or a prefers-reduced-motion media query) (MOT-6)
the hover lift is small (about 2px and one shadow step), not scale-105 with the largest shadow (VIS-8)
pressable controls compress slightly on press, scaling to about 0.95–0.98 (MOT-7)

evals.name: review-signup-form-usability
evals.prompt:
Review this sign-up form an AI generated and tell me what to fix.

- Three steps: details, phone, password. Going back to a step clears its fields.
- Fields have placeholder text ('Full name', 'Email') but no labels.
- Phone uses <input type="number" pattern="\d{10}"> and rejects '(386) 555-0100'.
- The password rules ('12+ characters, one number') appear only in a tooltip on an info icon.
- On an invalid submit, the bad fields get a red border and the form shakes for 800 ms. No message.
- The 'Create account' button does nothing visible for the 2–3 seconds the request takes.
- The close × in the corner is a 14px icon with no padding.
evals.expected_output: Findings keyed to rule IDs, most severe first, covering visible labels and kept input, forgiving phone input with one stored format, persistent password hints, errors in text with focus and announcement plus a short or no shake, a pending state on submit, and a bigger hit area for the close icon.

assertions.text: requires visible labels instead of placeholder-only fields (INT-5)
says going back must keep entered values (INT-5)
replaces type=number with a tel or text input that strips formatting, accepts '(386) 555-0100', and stores one normalised format (INT-6)
moves the password rules out of the tooltip so they stay visible beside the field (INT-5)
requires error text by each field, focus moved to the first invalid field, and an announcement; the shake is shortened to about 300 ms or dropped, and not played under reduced motion (MOT-8, MOT-6)
adds a pending state to 'Create account' that prevents a double submit (INT-4)
enlarges the close button's hit area to at least 24×24 CSS px, 44×44 on touch (INT-2)
uses the RULE-ID: problem → fix format and does not list passes

evals.name: motion-for-dense-admin-tool
evals.prompt: We're building an internal claims-processing dashboard. Each processor handles about 200 claims a day: search, open, approve or reject, next. Our designer wants to apply all 12 Disney animation principles to make it feel polished. Which should we use, and what else matters most for this app?
evals.expected_output: Keeps essential motion (transition by change, easing, short timing, press feedback, error and success feedback, reduced motion), skips expressive principles such as anticipation and arcs for a dense daily tool, and puts frequency of use, response time, targets, and conventions ahead of animation.

assertions.text: recommends short, purposeful motion only: easing, timing at the short end, and feedback (MOT-4, MOT-5, MOT-7 to MOT-9)
advises skipping or minimising anticipation and arcs (MOT-12, MOT-13) because they slow down a tool used hundreds of times a day
requires a reduced-motion fallback (MOT-6)
applies frequency of use: search and approve/reject one click away, keyboard shortcuts, remembered filters, and Undo instead of confirmation for reversible actions (INT-7)
addresses response feedback for actions that wait on the server (INT-4)
does not recommend applying all 12 principles

evals.name: sidebar-icon-sizing
evals.prompt: An AI tool built our app's sidebar: 14px labels with Tailwind's text-sm, icons at size={18} on Inbox and Projects, size={24} on Settings, and size={16} on Help, with a 12px gap between icon and label. Two items have no icon. It looks slightly off but we can't say why. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Ties every icon to the label's line height (20px for 14px text on a 20px line), centred on the line, with an 8px gap, gives every item an icon or none on one keyline, and keeps hit areas separate from icon size.

assertions.text: sizes every icon to the label's line height, 20 × 20 for 14px text on a 20px line (VIS-9)
sets the gap between icon and label to 8px (VIS-9)
gives every item an icon or none, on one left keyline (HIE-5, HIE-9, VIS-9)
keeps each row's hit area at least 44px tall on touch regardless of icon size (INT-2)
